America Gets a New Fiat Topolino, Plus One Built Like a Yacht
21 photos
Photo: Fiat
It's been only a few months since the Italian carmaker Fiat unloaded on American shores one of the smallest cars available at the moment on the market, the Topolino. The little mouse, as it's affectionately called (because that's what the term means in Italian), has proven so successful that the carmaker has now announced the 2027 variant, with a new body style taking center stage, plus a sort of concept car mimicking the feel of a yacht.
I'll start with the concept, if it can be called that, as it is, for all intents and purposes, the highlight of the announcement. The one-of-a-kind build was put together with Italian yacht maker Sanlorenzo , and it was shown in the metal during the Fort Lauderdale International Boat Show that kicked off this week.
Based on the standard electric vehicle, the unnamed design comes with a special interior taking cues and inspiration from Sanlorenzo’s ways of designing yacht interiors. That translates into natural materials and premium textiles used in abundance on the car's seats, dashboard, and sunroof. Why, even the seat belts are custom, and there is leather and nautical-grade wood spread all around.
Fiat did not say what will happen to the one-off design now that it's out and about, but we do know what the bulk of the Americans will get with their low-speed vehicle that's the craze of the neighborhood.
Until now, there were only two versions to choose from, the standard and Dolce Vita, but now a third model is joining the range: the Open Air featuring a soft-top rollback roof. Other than that, the newcomer is exactly the same as its siblings.
When it comes to the powertrain, that means a battery pack that's good for up to 46 miles (74 km) of range on a single charge, and an electric motor that can push it down the road at maximum speeds of 25 mph (40 kph) - hence the low-speed vehicle designation.
The 2027 Fiat Topolino range also gets treated to a new full-color digital cluster, and gets two new colors for the bodywork: Corallo Orange and Luna Greige. The unique Monsterlino, a sound system designed with sound specialist Monster, will also be offered soon for the range. The system is, technically, a grab-and-go affair that can be magnetically attached to the car when not in use in some other way, elsewhere.
Fiat said that the existing range, which launched earlier this summer, is already sold out at various dealers across the nation, and that's why it made the 2027 model year incarnation available as of right now.
The carmaker is selling the standard version for prices that start at $13,995, not including the destination fee. For that, it also throws in a complimentary home delivery, as long as home isn't more than 50 miles (80 km) from the dealer. A complimentary conversion kit to turn the car into a street-legal affair is also offered for the models already sold – the new ones are already configured this way.
